chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: Earlier 1940 Chicago sides: Chloe, Flingin' a Whing Ding, Kitty on Toast
summary: Titles recorded in Chicago include a slow 'Chloe' paired with John Kirby's swing side, Israel Crosby's 'Flingin' a Whing Ding', and 'Kitty on Toast' (named by Hammond), Ray Nance's violin feature over diminished chords on Honeysuckle Rose.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Then in -- earlier that year, you had apparently three or four different dates in Chicago with some -- I guess the earlier band, probably before you went to raid Nat Towles band. You have February 27, several things for Vocalion, I guess --
Yes. "Chloe." That was done May 8, in Chicago.

Of course, you know that was part one and part two. You know the band on the other side was John Kirby and that great little outfit that he had. Now we made a slow version of that with the big band, and John Kirby had the swing side.
You should have a tune there that featured Israel Crosby on bass called "Flinging a Whing Ding." (unintelligible)
There's -- I don't -- oh yes, that was in August of 1940, recorded in Chicago, and Israel Crosby -- yeah.
That was a classic. Then you should have one by Ray Nance, that he played his violin on. John Hammond named this tune, and I can't -- for the love of me, I can't recall it.

Well, some that are listed here for that date of August are "When Dreams Come True," "I Still Have My Dreams," "Turkey Special," "Coquette," "Flingin' a Whing-Ding." Then earlier in May -- or no, July, there's "Sultan" Serenade, "Ginger Bells," and "Do Re Mi."
It has you -- original by you?

This was a take off on Honeysuckle Rose that Ray Nance was playing the violin. Instead of using the regular chords to Honeysuckle Rose, to make it different, I used diminished chords, and he would run them on his fiddle. It was a great thing. I've got it! Kitty on Toast!
Okay. That was recorded in February.
John Hammond named that tune. Kitty on Toast. It just came to me. I've been trying to think of that for four or five days.
Based on a take off on Honeysuckle Rose.
